That hook takes one      adapter and one ABI-encoded `MarketParams` and is the right tool when the caller knows the market.      A curator vault lists many Morpho Blue markets and the list moves under the curator timelock, so      packing each market into its own hook call makes the strategy do the vault's job and the packed      params go stale. This hook reads the list on chain instead. Both are deployed and registered.data has the following structureTHIS NATSPEC IS THE SOURCE OF THE REGISTRY BUILD PATH, not just documentation. The OMS hook      registry parses the four lines above to derive:        None-bytes32-32-yieldSourceOracleId, None-address-20-yieldSource, None-uint256-32-assets,        None-bool-1-usePrevHookAmount      The field NAMES are load-bearing. `yieldSourceOracleId` must not be renamed to anything matching      the registry's reserved `^placeholder\\d*$` pattern, which is encoded `Zeroes-...` and would      zero-fill the oracle id before it ever reached the chain; and OMS asset identity reads the      parameter named literally `yieldSource`. Registry tags are set at registration, not here:      `yieldSourceOracleId` = get_oracle_id_from_vault, `yieldSource` = get_yield_source_from_vault,      `assets` = get_input_amount.`assets` IS UNDERLYING, NOT SHARES, and it is what lands in idle. The penalty is charged ON TOP, as      a share burn against the executing account, so idle rises by the full `assets` rather than by      `assets * (1 - penalty)`. The next hop is an ordinary ERC-4626 withdraw of that same number with      `usePrevHookAmount` FALSE.SCOPE LIMIT, AND ITS OPERATOR-FACING SYMPTOM. Only Morpho Blue market adapters are walked, one      level deep, never recursing into a `MorphoVaultV1Adapter` or any other adapter shape. A Vault V2      whose liquidity sits entirely behind non-market adapters therefore reverts `SHORTFALL(0, assets)`.      That looks like an outage and is not one: it is this hook declining to unwind an adapter type it      does not model. Unwinding those is explicitly out of scope.TRUST ASSUMPTION: Morpho Vault V2's internal reentrancy guards, its adapter registry and its own 2%      penalty ceiling are trusted. The adapter SET is curator-controlled, which is why every adapter is      identity-checked (`parentVault()`) and gas-stipended before it is read. `onBehalf` is always the      executing smart account.NOT A WITHDRAW, despite moving underlying. `forceDeallocate` moves underlying from an adapter into      the vault's idle balance and burns penalty shares from the executing account; it does not redeem      shares and does not pay the account. It stays NONACCOUNTING and the classification stays      config/instant/sized. amountRoles(bytes).details: DENOMINATION IS DELIBERATELY `TOKEN`, NOT `ASSETS`, matching the one-market sibling. By the      letter of `ISuperHook`'s own definitions `ASSETS` is the closer fit, since `assets` here is an      underlying quantity on an ERC-4626-shaped vault. It stays `TOKEN` because `ASSETS` invites OMS      to apply a price-per-share conversion, and there is no share conversion in this operation at      all. Changing it also requires an `amountMeta` override in `tooling/hook-enrichment.yaml`.The argument is intentionally unnamed and unread: `HookSizingInterface.t.sol` calls this with      `""`, so reading `data` here would break that caller.

params.data: The hook-specific calldata (same as passed to decodeAmounts)

returns.meta: Array of AmountMeta structs aligned index-by-index with decodeAmounts

build(address,address,bytes).details: Standard build pattern - MUST include preExecute first, postExecute last

params.account: The account to perform executions for (usually an ERC7579 account)
params.data: The hook-specific parameters and configuration data
params.prevHook: The address of the previous hook in the chain, or address(0) if first

returns.executions: Array of Execution structs defining calls to make

params.maxPenaltyWad_: Ceiling in WAD. Must be non-zero and at most `MORPHO_MAX_PENALTY_WAD`; a cap        above Morpho's own ceiling could never bind.
params.morpho_: The Morpho Blue singleton for this chain. Adapters pointing anywhere else are        skipped. Part of the CREATE2 address, so it cannot be repointed after deployment.

decodeAmounts(bytes).details: Used to determine the quantity of assets or shares being processed

returns.amounts: Array of amounts (length 1 for single-amount hooks, 2+ for compound hooks)

decodeUsePrevHookAmount(bytes).details: Used to create hook chains where output from one hook becomes input to the next

returns._0: True if the hook should use the previous hook's output amount

getOutAmount(address).details: This is the primary output value used by subsequent hooks

params.caller: The caller address for context identification

returns._0: The amount of tokens (assets or shares) processed

getOutToken(address).details: Used by subsequent hooks to determine what token the previous hook produced      PASSTHROUGH hooks auto-forward the previous hook's outToken      TRANSFORM hooks set this to their specific output token

params.caller: The caller address for context identification

returns._0: The address of the output token, or address(0) if not set

inspect(bytes).details: THE VAULT ALONE, deliberately. A leaf authorises this hook against one vault and does NOT pin      adapters or market ids, so a market the curator lists later is usable without re-signing — which      is the reason this hook reads the list on chain instead of taking it as calldata. `MAX_PENALTY_WAD`      and `MAX_MARKETS` are the bounds on that authority, and both are baked into the CREATE2 address.

returns._0: The arguments of the hook encoded

postExecute(address,address,bytes).details: Called after the main execution, used to update hook state and calculate results      Sets output values (outAmount, usedShares, etc.) for subsequent hooks

params.account: The account operations were performed for
params.data: The hook-specific parameters and configuration data
params.prevHook: The address of the previous hook in the chain, or address(0) if first

preExecute(address,address,bytes).details: Called before the main execution, used to validate inputs and set execution context      This method may perform state changes to set up the hook's execution state

params.account: The account to perform operations for
params.data: The hook-specific parameters and configuration data
params.prevHook: The address of the previous hook in the chain, or address(0) if first

replaceCalldataAmounts(bytes,uint256[]).details: Writes bytes 52..83 only — strictly below the flag at 84 — and the layout is fixed-length, so      the payload length is preserved.

params.amounts: The amounts to replace (must match length from decodeAmounts)
params.data: The data to replace amounts in

params.caller: The caller address for context identification

setExecutionContext(address).details: Used for security validation between preExecute and postExecute calls

params.caller: The caller address for context identification

setOutAmount(uint256,address).details: Used for updating `outAmount` when fees were deducted

params.caller: The caller address for context identification
params.outAmount: The amount of tokens processed by the hook

subtype().details: Used to categorize hooks beyond the basic HookType      For example, a hook might be of type INFLOW but subtype VAULT_DEPOSIT

returns._0: A bytes32 identifier for the specific hook functionality

supportsInterface(bytes4).details: Hooks that implement ISuperHookInflowOutflow/ISuperHookOutflow override      _supportsSizingInterface() to return true, which enables three-state detection:      S1: supportsInterface(ISuperHookInflowOutflow) == true → hook has sizing interface      S2: same as S1 but amountRoles(data).length == 0 → authoritatively sizeless      S3: supportsInterface(ISuperHookInflowOutflow) == false → legacy, no sizing interface

MAX_ADAPTERS().notice: Hard bound on how many registered adapters this hook will probe in one call.

MAX_MARKETS().notice: Hard bound on how many listed markets this hook will walk in one call.

MAX_PENALTY_WAD().notice: The highest `forceDeallocatePenalty` this hook will execute against, in WAD.

MORPHO().notice: The one Morpho Blue singleton this hook will read market state from.

MORPHO_MAX_PENALTY_WAD().notice: Morpho Vault V2's own hard ceiling on `forceDeallocatePenalty`, in WAD (2%).

SUB_TYPE().notice: The specific subtype identifier for this hook

amountRoles(bytes).notice: Returns per-slot metadata (direction + denomination) for each amount

asset().notice: The primary asset address this hook operates on

build(address,address,bytes).notice: Builds the execution array for the hook operation

decodeAmounts(bytes).notice: Extracts all amounts from the hook's calldata

decodeUsePrevHookAmount(bytes).notice: Determines if this hook should use the amount from the previous hook

description().notice: One-sentence description of what this hook does

executionNonce().notice: Execution nonce for creating unique contexts

getOutAmount(address).notice: The amount of tokens processed by the hook in a given caller context, subject to fees after update

getOutToken(address).notice: The output token address produced by the hook in a given caller context

hookType().notice: The type of hook (NONACCOUNTING, INFLOW, OUTFLOW)

setExecutionContext(address).notice: Sets the caller address that initiated the execution

setOutAmount(uint256,address).notice: Sets the output amount for the hook

spToken().notice: The special token address (if any) associated with this hook's operation

subtype().notice: Returns the specific subtype identification for this hook

usedShares().notice: The number of shares used by this hook's operation
